newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jordan's King Hussein on Israeli condolence call.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's King Hussein on Israeli condolence call.

text.p: Jordan's King Hussein flew to Israel on Sunday to pay condolences to the families of seven schoogirls killed by a Jordanian soldier and to try to defuse tensions with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
The king, a pilot, landed his own plane at Tel Aviv's Ben-Gurion airport at 12:46 a.m. (1046 GMT). Israeli television stations broadcast the landing live.

The monarch, accompanied by the commander-in-chief of Jordan's armed forces, shook hands with Netanyahu. It was their first meeting since a harsh exchange of letters last week over Israeli plans to build a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

After the landing, the two leaders rode by motorcade to the houses of the girls' families in the towns of Zlafon and Bet Shemesh. A Jordanian soldier slaughtered the girls while they were on an outing at the Israeli-Jordanian border on Thursday.
Israel vowed on Sunday to press ahead with the Jewish settlement despite the king's conciliatory visit and warnings by police the settlement would threaten Middle East peace moves.
